caption: Each cell is the measured all-zeros probability K(x, x′) = cos²(x − x′), so K(0, π/4) = 0.5. All three eigenvalues are positive, which makes this a valid kernel for the classical SVM.

spec.title: Kernel matrix K = cos²(x − x′)
spec.aria: A 3 by 3 kernel matrix for x equal to 0, pi/4 and pi/2, with entries 1, 0.5 and 0 from cos squared of x minus x prime; its eigenvalues 1.71, 1.00 and 0.29 are all positive, so the matrix is positive semidefinite and a classical SVM can use it.
